assumption_log.what: Data source is a single internal database or data warehouse with a defined schema
assumption_log.why: Reporting tools require a data source; without specification, assuming a standard internal database is the most common pattern for internal reporting projects
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline requires defined inputs and data sources
assumption_log.consequence: If data comes from multiple sources with different schemas or requires ETL transformation, architecture and Phase 2 effort doubles; project type may shift from TYPE_C (reporting) to TYPE_D (integration)
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows decomposition to proceed without stakeholder delay. Risks: if actual data source is complex (multiple systems, real-time streaming, unstructured data), timeline and team size estimates are invalid.

assumption_log.what: Success is measured by tool adoption and user satisfaction, not by specific KPIs (e.g., query response time, concurrent users, data freshness)
assumption_log.why: Input provides no quantitative success criteria; assuming adoption-based success is standard for internal tools
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted success criteria
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders expect specific performance targets (e.g., <2s query response, 100 concurrent users, real-time data), Phase 3 and Phase 4 effort increases significantly; may require infrastructure scaling or caching architecture not currently planned
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning without stakeholder re-alignment. Risks: if actual success criteria are performance-driven, team will discover this during UAT and may need to re-architect.

assumption_log.what: Team composition will be 1 Product Manager, 1 Data Engineer, 1 Backend Developer, 1 Frontend Developer, 1 QA Engineer (5 people total)
assumption_log.why: Input states 'team size TBD' but does not specify roles or count; assuming a standard TYPE_C (Data Pipeline/Reporting) team composition from knowledge base benchmarks
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to WBS and project type
assumption_log.consequence: If actual team is smaller (e.g., 2 developers), timeline extends 2-3x; if larger, budget increases. If team lacks data engineering expertise, Phase 2 and Phase 3 effort increases due to learning curve.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows task decomposition and critical path calculation. Risks: if actual team size or composition differs, entire schedule baseline becomes invalid.

assumption_log.what: Data source is accessible and documented; no data access permissions delays or compliance reviews required
assumption_log.why: Input does not mention access restrictions, compliance requirements, or data sensitivity; assuming standard internal data access
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline
assumption_log.consequence: If data access requires security review, compliance approval, or cross-team coordination, Phase 1 extends by 2-4 weeks; if data is sensitive (PII, financial), security architecture and Phase 3 effort increases
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 1 to be short (1-2 weeks). Risks: if data access is restricted or compliance-gated, project stalls in Phase 1.

assumption_log.what: Reporting tool is a web-based dashboard (browser-based, not mobile app, not desktop application)
assumption_log.why: Input does not specify platform; web dashboard is the standard delivery format for internal reporting tools
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline requires defined delivery format
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders expect mobile app or desktop application, Phase 2 effort increases; if both web and mobile required, team size must increase or timeline extends
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows technology stack selection (standard web stack). Risks: if actual requirement is multi-platform, architecture and effort estimates are understated.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Data Engineer and Backend Developer must be full-time on critical path; Frontend Developer and QA Engineer have some scheduling flexibility but cannot be shared with other projects during Phases 2-4.

risk_register.description: If reporting requirements remain undefined (filter criteria, chart types, data dimensions not specified), then stakeholders will discover misalignment during Phase 2 demo and request significant rework, causing schedule slip and scope creep.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 internal demo reveals stakeholder expectations do not match built features; feedback requests major UI or data changes
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct detailed requirements workshop in Phase 1 (T2) with all stakeholders present; document specific filter criteria, chart types, and success metrics in writing before Phase 2 begins; obtain written sign-off
risk_register.contingency: If misalignment discovered in Phase 2 demo, pause development and conduct scope re-alignment workshop; adjust timeline and budget based on scope changes

risk_register.description: If data source is complex (multiple systems, real-time streaming, unstructured data, or requires ETL transformation), then Phase 2 data ingestion effort (T6) will exceed estimate by 50-100%, and project type may shift from TYPE_C (reporting) to TYPE_D (integration), requiring additional integration specialist and extending timeline.
risk_register.trigger: Data source audit (T1) reveals multiple source systems, real-time data requirements, or complex schema transformations not anticipated
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct thorough data source audit in Phase 1 (T1) before any development; document data volume, freshness requirements, and transformation complexity; identify any external system dependencies early
risk_register.contingency: If data source is more complex than assumed, add Data Engineer capacity or extend Phase 2 timeline by 2-3 weeks; escalate to stakeholder for scope/timeline trade-off decision

risk_register.description: If team size is smaller than assumed (fewer than 5 people or any role part-time), then critical path tasks (T8, T12, T18) will be delayed, and overall project timeline will extend by 2-3 weeks or more.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder confirms team size is fewer than 5 people, or any critical path role (Frontend Developer, Backend Developer, Data Engineer) is allocated less than 80% to this project
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm team composition and allocation percentages in writing before Phase 1 begins; ensure all critical path roles are full-time (80%+); identify backup resources for key roles
risk_register.contingency: If team is smaller than assumed, reduce scope (defer advanced charting or filtering features to Phase 2 release) or extend timeline by 2-3 weeks

risk_register.description: If success criteria are performance-driven (e.g., <2s query response, 100 concurrent users, real-time data freshness) rather than adoption-based, then Phase 3 optimization (T12) and Phase 4 performance testing (T17) effort will increase significantly, and infrastructure scaling may be required.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder specifies performance targets during Phase 1 requirements (T2) that were not mentioned in original brief; or Phase 4 performance testing (T17) reveals actual load exceeds assumptions
risk_register.mitigation: Explicitly ask stakeholders in Phase 1 (T2) about performance expectations, concurrent user targets, and data freshness requirements; document these as non-functional requirements before Phase 2 begins
risk_register.contingency: If performance targets are higher than assumed, add caching layer, database optimization, or infrastructure scaling; extend Phase 3 and Phase 4 by 1-2 weeks

risk_register.description: If data access requires security review, compliance approval, or cross-team coordination (e.g., data governance, PII handling), then Phase 1 will extend by 2-4 weeks, blocking Phase 2 start.
risk_register.trigger: Data source audit (T1) reveals data is sensitive (PII, financial, regulated), or data access requires approval from security/compliance team; approval process takes longer than 1 week
risk_register.mitigation: Identify data sensitivity and access requirements in Phase 1 (T1); initiate security/compliance review in parallel with requirements definition (T2); confirm access permissions before Phase 2 begins
risk_register.contingency: If access approval is delayed, conduct Phase 2 development with sample/test data and defer production data integration to Phase 3; adjust timeline accordingly

risk_register.description: If this is the team's first reporting tool project or first use of the selected charting library, then Phase 2 development (T8, T9) will take longer due to learning curve, and technical debt may accumulate.
risk_register.trigger: Team members report unfamiliarity with charting library or reporting tool architecture during Phase 2 kickoff; development velocity is slower than estimated
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct technology spike in Phase 1 (T5) to validate charting library and architecture; allocate 20% buffer to Phase 2 development tasks; pair experienced and junior developers
risk_register.contingency: If learning curve is steeper than expected, extend Phase 2 by 1 week or reduce scope of advanced charting features

risk_register.description: If stakeholders expect mobile app or multi-platform support (not just web dashboard), then Phase 2 development effort increases significantly, and team size must increase or timeline extends.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests mobile app or tablet-specific features during Phase 1 requirements (T2) or Phase 2 demo (T10); current plan assumes web-only
risk_register.mitigation: Explicitly confirm platform requirements in Phase 1 (T2); document that initial release is web-only; defer mobile to Phase 2 release if requested
risk_register.contingency: If mobile is required for launch, add Frontend Developer capacity or extend Phase 2 by 2-3 weeks

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements definition (T2) is incomplete or stakeholder is unavailable for sign-off, then Phase 2 development will proceed with ambiguous requirements, leading to rework and schedule slip.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 (T2) extends beyond 2 weeks due to stakeholder unavailability or conflicting priorities; requirements document is not signed off before Phase 2 begins
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule Phase 1 requirements workshop (T2) early; confirm stakeholder availability for sign-off; use written requirements document as gate before Phase 2 kickoff
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 extends, delay Phase 2 start rather than proceeding with incomplete requirements; adjust overall timeline

risk_register.description: If data handled by the reporting tool is subject to compliance requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2) not mentioned in the brief, then security review (T14) and Phase 3 effort will increase, and compliance audit may be required before launch.
risk_register.trigger: Data source audit (T1) or stakeholder reveals data is subject to regulatory requirements; security review (T14) identifies compliance gaps
risk_register.mitigation: Ask stakeholders in Phase 1 (T1) about data sensitivity and regulatory requirements; identify any compliance obligations before Phase 2 begins
risk_register.contingency: If compliance requirements are discovered late, conduct compliance audit in Phase 4; defer launch if necessary to remediate gaps

staffing_plan.notes: Owns requirements definition (T2), internal demo (T10), UAT (T16), documentation (T18), and go-live sign-off (T20). Must be available for stakeholder alignment throughout project.
Owns data source audit (T1), schema design (T3), data ingestion (T6), data quality validation (T11), and performance testing (T17). Must be full-time during Phases 1-3.
Owns architecture (T5), API implementation (T7), performance optimization (T12), security review (T14), and deployment (T19). Critical path tasks T5, T12, T18 cannot slip.
Owns UI wireframes (T4), dashboard UI (T8), charting integration (T9), and edge case testing (T13). Critical path task T8 cannot slip; must be full-time during Phases 2-3.
Owns edge case testing (T13) and comprehensive testing (T15). QA effort is 72h / 280h dev hours = 25.7% of development effort, meeting PMBOK 8.2 minimum. Critical path task T15 cannot slip.

open_questions.question: What is the specific data source for this reporting tool? Is it a single database, multiple systems, real-time streaming data, or unstructured data? What is the data volume and freshness requirement?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If data source is complex (multiple systems, real-time, ETL-heavy), project type shifts from TYPE_C to TYPE_D, requiring different team composition and architecture. Phase 2 effort could double.

open_questions.question: What are the specific success criteria for this reporting tool? Are they adoption-based (% of team using it), performance-based (query response time, concurrent users), or business-outcome-based (decisions made faster)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If success criteria are performance-driven, Phase 3 and Phase 4 effort increases significantly. If adoption-based, current plan is defensible.

open_questions.question: What is the confirmed team composition and allocation? How many people are available, and what are their roles and full-time/part-time allocations?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If team is smaller than 5 people or any role is part-time, timeline extends 2-3 weeks. Current plan assumes 5 full-time people.

open_questions.question: Are there any compliance, security, or data sensitivity requirements? Is the data subject to GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, or other regulatory frameworks?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If data is sensitive or regulated, Phase 1 extends for security/compliance review, and Phase 3 security effort increases. Current plan assumes standard internal data.

open_questions.question: Who is the named stakeholder or Product Owner responsible for approving scope, timeline, and budget decisions? Is there a single decision-maker or multiple stakeholders?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If multiple stakeholders with conflicting priorities, scope creep and schedule slip risk increases. Current plan assumes single stakeholder alignment.
